DEVICE DESCRIPTION
The HAMILTON-Cl is designed for adults and pediatrics requiring invasive or noninvasive
ventilation support. The HAMILTON-Cl ventilator covers a full range of clinical
requirements: including invasive ventilation, automated ventilation with Adaptive Support
Ventilation (ASV), and Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV).
The HAMILTON-Cl is suitable for ICU special-care areas, cardiac surgery recovery rooms,
stepdown or sub-acute care units, and long-term care centers. With its IntelliTrig technology,
the HAMILTON-Cl responds to the changing breathing patterns or circuit leaks found in
non-invasive ventilation by automatically varying leaks and adapting sensitivity thresholds
for optimal response to the patient's breath.
The HAMILTON-Cl's software and ventilation modes are identical to the HAMILTON-fl's
software and ventilation modes. One can operate the HAMILTON-Cl with the touchscreen
or with a single turn wheel. Hard keys give direct access to the most important functions. In
effect, the HAMILTON-Cl is a HAMILTON-Ti, but with the features related to transport-
ventilation stripped off.
With the large alarm lamp, a clinician can immediately identify an alarming HAMILTON-Cl
ventilator because of the alarm lamp located at the top of the device, even if the clinician is
at a long distance away or when several different devices are operating simultaneously in
the same room.
Interface for POMS, patient monitor, and nurse call are available as well. The optional
interfaces provide ports for connection to hospital monitors, Patient Data Management
Systems (POMS), and nurse call systems.
The high-performance turbine can deliver up to 210 L/min flow; this relatively high flow rate
is potentially helpful when utilizing NIV modes of ventilation.
INTENDED USE
The HAMILTON-Cl ventilator is intended to provide positive pressure ventilatory support
to adults and pediatrics.
Intended areas of use:
* In the intensive care ward or in the recovery room.
* During transfer of ventilated patients within the hospital.
The HAMILTON-Cl ventilator is a medical device intended for use by qualified, trained
personnel under the direction of a physician and within the limits of its stated technical
specifications.

DISCUSSION ON THE NON-CLINICAL TESTS
The non-clinical test results show that the HAMILTON-Cl is safe and effective for its
intended use. Below is a list of standards and guidance documents recognized by FDA to
establish the basis of safety and effectiveness for the HAMILTON-Cl. These standards are

related standards, such as the RTCA/DO 160F, which the HAMILTON-Cl is not designed
for. The results of the following non-clinical tests support a determination of substantial
equivalence. In addition, the conclusions drawn from the non-clinical tests demonstrate that
the device is as safe, as effective, and performs just as well as the predicate device.

The intended use statement for the HAMILTON-Cl ventilator is comparable to the predicate
device. The only difference is that the HAMILTON-Cl has a more limited intended use due
to the fact that it is not hardened for transport environments. However, the technological
characteristics (i.e., design, material, energy source) and performance specifications of the
HAMI LTON-Cl ventilator are equivalent to those of the predicate device. The HAM ILTON-
Cl meets all the standards set by FDA for non-transport ventilators. The differences do not
affect the safety and effectiveness of the device when used as labeled.
The intended use of the HAMILTON-Cl is covered by the referenced predicate device. The
technical characteristics of the HAMILTON-Cl do not raise any new questions regarding the
safety or effectiveness of ventilators. The HAMILTON-Cl's software has gone through
verification/validation tests. A complete revision level history, hazard analysis, and a
traceability analysis linking requirements to validation were done. The conclusions drawn
from the non-clinical tests demonstrate that the HAMILTON-Cl is as safe, as effective, and
performs as well as the legally marketed device. The differences are not critical to the
intended therapeutic use of the device. The HAMILTON-Cl is, therefore, considered to be
substantially equivalent to the currently marketed predicate device which has been
previously cleared by FDA.
